docs.text: Zebrasoma gemmatum ¶ Result: fail ¶ Arrival Notes / Origin / Price ¶ Vibrant corals and fish, $147.50 One of the nicest gem tangs I've seen. Looks great, but has a pinched belly. Yet another awesome fish from Vibrant! Initial diagnoses ¶ Possible internal parasites, but should not be too much of an issue. Initial prognosis ¶ Should be a straightforward QT. Day 1 ¶ Drip acclimated, then gave the fish an H2O2 bath. Fed the fish, and he ate a bit of the food, but not very aggressively. Dosed up copper, and noticed a couple spots on the fish, but not a concerning amount. Day 2 ¶ Woke up and checked on him. Found him laying on the floor of the tank, completely covered in spots. Eyes are cloudy, and the fish looks completely morribund. We created a makeshift oxygen generator with potatos + hydrogen peroxide to help him breathe. A few hours after adding some O2, he can swim on his own for a brief period of time. video When we went to bed, he seemed like he was in a decent state. I am optimistic he will recover. Day 3 ¶ Woke up to find the tang did not make it through the night. Very disappointing, but Danelle will replace him (even though I didn't ask her to). I look forward to the next one, but will be starting him in full copper immediately instead of waiting for a few hours. Conclussions: ¶ Given the timeline of this fish's demise, I think this guy suffered from marine velvet. I was very impressed by how effective the potato oxygen was, and may use this trick in the future if a similar situation is encountered. Similar fish: ¶ n / a

docs.text: Zebrasoma rostratum ¶ Result: fail ¶ Arrival Notes / Origin / Price ¶ SDC, $499 (sale price) Rather large, adult specimen. Specimen came in 3 gallons of (pretty dirty) water bag was lined with korean newspaper, I wonder if he was drop-shipped. Initial diagnoses ¶ Has some ich visible, but a manageable amount Belly is definitely pinched, which makes me very nervous Initial prognosis ¶ While the pinched belly is pretty worrying, I'm optimistic. Day 1 ¶ Specimen arrived via AA cargo, after ~12 hours transit. After drip acclimation, he was placed in a methylene blue + formalin bath for 30 minutes After bath, placed in a tank by himself with air stone + PVC + sponge filter Due to visible ich, I pre-dosed the water to 2.5 ppm copper + 300 mg nitrofurazone. Fed brine shrimp soaked in metro / kanaplex. He ate somewhat well, but not super aggresively. this inspired confidence, as he ate in full copper + ate medicated video here . Due to SDC reputation for uronema, I dosed formalin at night Day 2 ¶ Eating less aggressively, possibly not at all. Breathing seems labored, but not aggressive. The water is somewhat cloudy, so I performed a 5 gallon water change, pre-dosed with copper + sucked out as much food as I could from the bottom Day 3 ¶ Still not eating much, but the food seems to disappear. I added nori on a clip to see if he'd go for that, but he seemed disinterested. He swims around in a pattern: leave PVC towards the center, swim up a bit, turn around, swim through PVC, rotate (awkwardly) in the corner, and repeat. Day 4 ¶ Woke up around 6 AM for a frag swap, came down to find the tang dead. He was floating at the top of the tank with his mouth facing up. He was alive and looking normal when Ruxin added prazipro before we went to bed ~1 AM. I unfortunately didn't look at the fish before I went upstairs, as I was focused on the swap. Conclussions: ¶ I'm not sure what happened, honestly. I never saw any tang poops. I saw some stringy white excriment leaving him, but it was not long enough for me to think internal worms. Most likely internal flagellates. Other than disease, ammonia could have played a factor. The fact that this guy died at night and was found at the surface could mean lack of O2, but I did not see unusual breathing from this guy, other than the somewhat labored breathes. Similar fish: ¶ This one reminded me of the first time we QT'd a gem tang .
